---
title: "Scenarios"
---

The scenarios are designed for in-person practice with the Zoll. Use the public slides for learner review; facilitator-specific prompts belong in the instructor guide.

Each case now includes a brief resident/nurse-team interface prompt: who has bedside context, what the resident should ask, and how the plan should be closed-looped.

<div class="scenario-card">
<h3>Defibrillator Simulator</h3>
<p>Practice manual defibrillator workflow before the cases: pad placement, synchronized cardioversion, defibrillation, and transcutaneous pacing on a 3D virtual patient.</p>
<p><a href="https://simulation.health.ufl.edu/education-training/online-simulations/defibrillator-simulator/">Open simulator</a></p>
</div>

::: {.scenario-grid}
::: {.scenario-card}
### Case 1

Code blue for an unresponsive patient with no pulse. Focus: rhythm-check process, uncertainty, and using recorder/timekeeper input.

[Open case](slides/case_1.html)
:::

::: {.scenario-card}
### Case 2

Telemetry-triggered code blue on hospital day 2. Focus: first rhythm decision, team timing, and immediate post-ROSC priorities.

[Open case](slides/case_2.html)
:::

::: {.scenario-card}
### Case 3

Young patient collapses on telemetry after receiving several inpatient medications. Focus: rhythm recognition, medication-history input, and choosing the safest immediate action.

[Open case](slides/case_3.html)
:::

::: {.scenario-card}
### Case 4

RRT for a hospitalized patient with a very fast heart rate. Focus: stability assessment, bedside/outreach story, and deciding whether rhythm-specific treatment or escalation is needed.

[Open case](slides/case_4.html)
:::

::: {.scenario-card}
### Case 5

RRT for bradycardia with hypotension and confusion. Focus: preparing the room, equipment, and team before further deterioration.

[Open case](slides/case_5.html)
:::
:::
